Another Russian refinery goes offline: Volgograd plant shuts down completely after Ukrainian drone attack, Reuters reports
October 6, 2026, 7:48 pm
Source: Reuters
An oil refinery in Volgograd has stopped all crude oil processing after a Ukrainian drone attack on October 2, Reuters reported, citing sources.
The news agency gave no further details.
Volgograd Governor Andrey Bocharov said there had been a “massive drone attack on industrial infrastructure” but did not specify which facilities were targeted. Eyewitnesses posted photos and videos of a large fire in the area around the Volgograd refinery.
Ukrainian drones previously attacked the Volgograd refinery on May 29 and July 31, Reuters reported. According to the website of its owner, Lukoil, the refinery can process about 14 million metric tons of crude oil a year — roughly 5% of Russia’s total refining volume.

President Vladimir Putin has ordered Russian Railways to give priority to export grain shipments across the national rail network as Ukrainian drone attacks cut off southern shipping hubs, the Kommersant newspaper reported Tuesday.
Standard Russian Railways rules generally prioritize domestic freight and transit shipments over export goods. Now, grain trains can leapfrog other export commodities like coal on congested rail routes leading to Baltic and Arctic ports.
“Regarding commercial shipping in the Black Sea, the president indeed instructed the Agriculture Ministry together with other agencies to work out alternative delivery routes for domestic grain to world markets,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told the publication.
Grain has been moved into the third-highest priority category on Russia’s railway system, which is reserved for cargo transported under direct presidential orders.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday that Lithuania’s move, alongside broader plans to expand US and NATO military infrastructure in the region, risked further escalating tensions.
Lithuania has taken a step towards removing a constitutional ban on nuclear weapons from its territory, bringing the Baltic state closer to the legal position of its neighbours as European allies debate how to strengthen NATO’s deterrence in the face of Russia.

vyrez.text:
Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason - BBC News
Image source, AP
Image caption, Agents arrested August Hanning (pictured from 2015) at his home on Tuesday
By Olivia Ireland
Published
3 hours ago
Former German spy chief August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.
Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.
Prosecutors allege that he used classified intelligence to "draft an analysis" for one foreign intelligence service and maintained contact with another foreign spying service. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.
Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D, accusing him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents for money.
Manfred D, who was Hanning's bureau chief and remained in the BND until this year, is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
Local media reported Hanning was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near Münster while Manfred D was arrested in Bavaria.…

titulek: Former German spy chief arrested for treason and espionage
titulekPuvodni: Former German spy chief arrested for treason and espionage
shrnuti: The allegations amount to a huge embarrassment for Berlin's foreign intelligence agency.

vyrez.text:
Former German spy chief arrested for treason and espionage – POLITICO
Skip to main content
Advertisement
BERLIN — A former head of Germany’s foreign intelligence agency was arrested early Tuesday in connection with an investigation into suspected espionage and attempted treason, according to the German Federal Prosecutors Office.
An informant allegedly provided August Hanning, the former head of the foreign intelligence agency, or BND, with nearly two thousand documents, many of them classified, according to a statement from federal prosecutors . In one case, Hanning used classified information provided by an informant identified as Manfred D. to create an analysis for an employee of a foreign intelligence service, according the prosecutors office.
“The accused Hanning is under strong suspicion of espionage constituting treason,” the prosecutors’ statement read.
The allegations will amount to a huge embarrassment for Germany’s foreign intelligence agency, which Hanning ran between 1998 and 2005.
This is a developing story.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea.
The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.
Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died.
Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea.

A bomb destroyed a car belonging to a participant in Russia’s war against Ukraine on October 2 in Novomoskovsk, in Russia’s Tula region, the Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported.
The bomb had been planted under the car’s chassis, according to  data from the anonymous Russian Telegram channel VChK-OGPU. The driver killed was identified as Roman Syromyatnikov, and the Novomoskovsk-based news outlet Novomoskovsk Segodnya confirmed the death of a person by that name.
Syromyatnikov worked at Russia’s Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN) facilities in the Tula region during the 2010s. Source: Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces
A Russian military Mi-8 helicopter entered Polish airspace on September 23 at 11:08 a.m., the operational command of the Polish army said.
The helicopter, flying from the Kaliningrad region, crossed about 300 meters (984 feet) into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds, the Polish military said.
Poland scrambled fighter jets and put ground forces and equipment on alert. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense,” the command said.
Russia has not yet commented on the incident.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on September 17 that Russia is planning “hybrid” strikes using missiles and drones against countries that support Ukraine. He claimed that “there is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles may fly into the territory of one or more NATO countries on the eastern flank, even cause destruction.”

NATO pracuje na strategii, jejímž cílem je dosáhnout rychlého vítězství v případě ruského útoku na východní křídlo aliance. Důraz přitom klade na integraci nových technologií, jako jsou drony a umělá inteligence, do tradičních vojenských schopností. Informovala o tom agentura Bloomberg.

Fico může z NATO odejít, říká polský exprezident. A přidává…

Moskva a přilehlá Moskevská oblast v noci na úterý čelily mohutnému ukrajinskému dronovému útoku. Informoval o něm moskevský starosta Sergej Sobjanin, podle kterého na oblast celkem udeřilo 650 ukrajinských dronů. Tento počet nebyl zatím potvrzen.
Foto: X.com/Nayika
Následky ukrajinského dronového útoku na Moskevskou oblast
Článek
Sobjanin sice informoval o mohutném útoku, ale, jak bývá u ruských úřadů běžné, nezmínil žádný zásah. Podle jeho vyjádření v noci ruští záchranáři zasahovali jen u spadlých trosek sestřelených dronů, píše server Ukrajinska pravda .
O škodách naopak informoval gubernátor Moskevské oblasti Andrej Vorobjov, podle kterého si údery vyžádaly jednoho mrtvého a nejméně šest zraněných. Zmínil také poškozené domy a vytlučená okna.

Vasilyev took over at Patriot Park in March 2026. One of his predecessors, Vyacheslav Akhmedov, also faced criminal prosecution: He was detained in 2024 and sentenced to five years in prison in 2025. Akhmedov was convicted of taking part in the theft of 25 million rubles. Businessman Oleg Varyukhin, who traveled to Russia after living in Ukraine for 27 years, has been charged with treason for paying Ukraine’s mandatory military levy into its state budget, Mediazona reported.
Varyukhin was detained in May 2026. In early August, his lawyer, Yuri Shel, said the treason charge stemmed from tax payments in Ukraine. At the time, it was unclear which tax the Russian authorities had taken issue with.
Officers from Russia’s Federal Security Service found records of the tax payments on Varyukhin’s phone during a search at the airport, his lawyer said.
Money transfers to support the Ukrainian army have previously led to treason prosecutions in Russia. But Varyukhin is the first person known to be prosecuted for treason for paying taxes into Ukraine’s state budget, Mediazona noted.

Kaliningrad, the militarized Russian exclave wedged between NATO and EU members Poland and Lithuania and a constant flashpoint between the Kremlin and the Atlantic Alliance, has become the center of Vladimir Putin’s nuclear threat against Europeans . Last week Moscow accused NATO of seeking to block Kaliningrad and threatened to use nuclear weapons if the military organization moves forward with that alleged plan. Na tradičním setkání se studenty, tentokrát v Bánovcích nad Bebravou, řekl: „Neblázněme! Buďme rádi, že na Slovensku žijeme v klidu, že nám na hlavy nepadají rakety a naše děti mohou bezpečně chodit do školy.“ Řekl to jen den po útoku ve škole ve Staškově. A rocky outpost of Italy in the Tyrrhenian Sea, the island of Ustica owes its name to the smouldering volcanic lava that gave its striking rock formations their dark hue.

Russland intensiviert seine hybride Kriegsführung mitten in Europa und testet gezielt die roten Linien der NATO. Doch was passiert, wenn ein solcher Anschlag auf deutschem Boden tatsächlich gelingt und den Bündnisfall auslöst? Im Gespräch analysiert Carlo, warum Putin gerade jetzt risikofreudiger wird und weshalb Friedrich Merz in der deutschen Debatte als entscheidender Schutzwall für weitere Hilfen gilt. Ukrainian drone attacks hit Volgograd and Samara, setting a refinery and a major oil tank farm on fire
October 2, 2026, 7:02 am
Source: Meduza
Ukrainian drones struck Volgograd and Samara overnight on October 2. Andrey Bocharov, governor of the Volgograd region, said there had been a “massive drone attack on industrial infrastructure” but did not specify which facilities had been targeted. He said a residential building caught fire and one person was injured.
Photos and videos posted by eyewitnesses showed a large fire in the area of the Volgograd oil refinery and the Kaustik chemical plant, Astra reported . Ukrainian drones have attacked the refinery several times before. Astra also reported that city residents said no drone alert had been issued in Volgograd.
An oil pipeline operations and dispatch facility in Samara caught fire, according to Astra. The Samara station is Europe’s largest oil storage tank complex and part of Transneft’s network. Four pipelines carry oil to it from Western Siberia, Tatarstan, the Orenburg region, and Kazakhstan.

Letecký útok na Pearl Harbor je pro Američany stále trauma. Což je patrné i z děje nové knihy Danielle Steelové Létající andělé. Pro našince je zase traumatem Mnichov 1938. Právě v této době se odehrává příběh mladé dívky Josefíny v díle Štěpána Javůrka. Básník Rainer Maria Rilke stále patří k oblíbeným autorům, což bezpochyby podpoří i jeho sbírka básní Okna plná dálek. Dále máme v nabídce publikaci o historii Krakonoše, atlas plazů i knihu věnující se jednomu tabuizovanému tématu, totiž bolesti.

Píše se rok 1941 a v důsledku drtivých ztrát na životech po japonském útoku na Pearl Harbor pocítí kamarádky Audrey a Lizzie zoufalství, protože obě ztratily blízkou osobu. Zatímco se vyrovnávají se svým zármutkem, sílí jejich odhodlání sehrát ve válečném úsilí významnou roli. Tyto vyškolené zdravotní sestry se přihlásí jako dobrovolnice k vojenské letecké záchranné jednotce a jsou vyslány…

titulek: Drones attack Russia's Volgograd: fires reported near oil refinery and chemical plant – video
titulekPuvodni: Drones attack Russia's Volgograd: fires reported near oil refinery and chemical plant – video
shrnuti: Explosions were heard in Volgograd overnight, while the glow from a fire was seen near the Volgograd oil refinery and Kaustik chemical plant. The cause of the fire remains unclear.

vyrez.text:
Drone attack reported in Volgograd, Russia, with fire seen near oil refinery and chemical plant | Ukrainska Pravda
A fire. Screenshot
Explosions were heard in the Russian city of Volgograd on the night of 1-2 October, while the glow from a fire was seen near an oil refinery and the Kaustik chemical plant.
Source: Russian media outlet Astra; Volgograd Oblast Governor Andrei Bocharov ; Exilenova+ Telegram channel
Details: Astra said that residents of Volgograd had reported drones and several explosions in different parts of the city overnight. They also complained that no air-raid warning had been issued.
Advertisement:





After analysing eyewitness footage, Astra determined that the glow from the fire could be seen coming from the direction of the Volgograd oil refinery and the nearby Kaustik plant. However, the available footage does not make it possible to determine what exactly caught fire.
Exilenova+ reported that explosions could be heard for a long time both in the city itself and in the industrial area of the Volgograd oil refinery.
Bocharov said the region's industrial infrastructure had come under a large-scale drone attack, but did not report any fires at the…

vyrizeni.poznamka: Ukrajinský dron/útok na cíl uvnitř Ruska (rafinerie, sklad); obě strany uvnitř probíhající války, bez doloženého následku pro sledované země. Požáry u rafinerie a chemičky ve Volgogradu.

titulek: Kyiv closes Pivdennyi and Paton bridges after Russian attack, restricts traffic on Metro Bridge
titulekPuvodni: Kyiv closes Pivdennyi and Paton bridges after Russian attack, restricts traffic on Metro Bridge
shrnuti: Kyiv authorities have closed the Pivdennyi and Paton bridges in both directions and restricted traffic towards the right bank on Metro Bridge following the Russian attack on 2 October.

vyrez.text:
Kyiv closes Pivdennyi and Paton bridges after Russian attack, limits traffic on Metro Bridge | Ukrainska Pravda
A bridge. Photo: TOV-TOB.livejournal.com
Kyiv has closed the Pivdennyi and Paton bridges in both directions, while traffic on the Metro Bridge is restricted towards the right bank following the Russian attack on the night of 1-2 October. Several bus and trolleybus routes have been changed as a result.
Source: Kyiv City Military Administration
Quote: "Public transport movement has been temporarily restricted on several bridges due to the overnight enemy attacks.
Advertisement:





The Pivdennyi Bridge is closed in both directions.
The Paton Bridge is closed in both directions. The Metro Bridge is closed towards the right bank."
Details: The restrictions are temporary. Kyivpastrans, a Kyiv transport company, is asking passengers to take the changes into account when planning their journeys.
Background:
Russian forces hit Kyiv's Pivdennyi Bridge again on the night of 1-2 October. A 25-storey residential building was also damaged in the Darnytskyi district, with information about casualties still being confirmed.
Debris damaged windows in a non-residential building and…

titulek: How a failed attack in Leipzig revealed a wider Russian campaign of attacks
titulekPuvodni: How a failed attack in Leipzig revealed a wider Russian campaign of attacks
shrnuti: Documents obtained by the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network trace drone bombs, incendiary parcels and arson attacks to Russian intelligence.

vyrez.text:
How a failed attack in Leipzig revealed a wider Russian campaign of attacks – POLITICO
Skip to main content
Advertisement
BERLIN — If the explosive had actually detonated, investigators might not have gotten their clearest look yet at what European officials believe is a wider Russian campaign of attacks.
On Aug. 4, a drone struck the wing of a Ukrainian aircraft at Germany’s Leipzig Airport and fell onto the tarmac. Strapped beneath it was a tin can packed with explosives. The device remained intact.
That gave investigators something unusually valuable: the bomb itself. The can was sealed with a metal plate stamped with seven circular indentations, according to an investigative file from German federal police reviewed by the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network.
Advertisement
It wasn’t the first time such an improvised explosive had been discovered on European soil. Almost two years earlier, on Aug. 20, 2024, police investigators arrived at a cemetery in Kaunas, Lithuania, with a bomb disposal team. They had received a highly sensitive tip from Poland concerning explosives and a Ukrainian man alleged to have deposited them there for Russian intelligence, according to…

Europe’s gray-zone war with Russia is getting harder to ignore.
Sarah Wheaton speaks to security expert and author Elisabeth Braw about how Europe should respond as sabotage, arson, cyberattacks and attacks on critical infrastructure become more frequent and more dangerous, who pays when businesses are targeted, and what happens when one of them turns deadly.
They also discuss Braw’s new book, The Undersea War: The International Battle for Supremacy at the Bottom of the World , and the increasingly contested cables, pipelines and infrastructure hidden beneath the seabed — another target in this growing gray-zone conflict.
You can read Elisabeth’s most recent column for POLITICO about how European businesses are paying the cost for Russias hybrid war here .
